definitions.explanation: The act of succeeding to a position, right, obligation, or property from a predecessor. Used primarily in legal and formal contexts.

examples.japanese: {事業|じぎょう}を{承継|しょうけい}する。
{父|ちち}から{権利|けんり}を{承継|しょうけい}した。
examples.english: I inherited the rights from my father.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}の{合併|がっぺい}により、すべての{債務|さいむ}は{新会社|しんがいしゃ}に{承継|しょうけい}される。
examples.english: Due to the merger, all debts will be succeeded to by the new company.

notes:
A compound of {承|しょう} (to receive, accept) and {継|けい} (to succeed, continue). This is a formal, primarily legal term for succession of rights, duties, property, or positions.

Used extensively in legal documents, corporate law, and official contexts. In everyday conversation, {引|ひ}き{継|つ}ぐ or {受|う}け{継|つ}ぐ would be used instead.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {事業|じぎょう}{承継|しょうけい}: business succession
- {権利|けんり}の{承継|しょうけい}: succession of rights
- {地位|ちい}の{承継|しょうけい}: succession to a position
- {包括|ほうかつ}{承継|しょうけい}: universal succession

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {継承|けいしょう}: inheritance, succession — more broadly used for traditions, culture, and techniques as well as legal matters
- {相続|そうぞく}: inheritance — specifically the legal inheritance of property after death
- {引|ひ}き{継|つ}ぎ: handover, taking over — everyday word for passing on work or responsibilities
